content: To begin, access the Patient Information Page template. This template is specifically designed to be user-friendly and should be used as the standard format for all coding. Replace the placeholder text Type page name here with the name of the condition you are working on. Additionally, wherever the word (condition) appears, substitute it with the name of the specific condition. Important Notes: 1. If the patient information page is derived from a well-established chapter, include the coding for the expanded navigation template. 2. Check the WikiDoc condition's main page to copy the appropriate InfoBox links. The InfoBox contains essential resources such as ICD10, ICD9, ICD0, OMIM, MedlinePlus, eMedicineSubj, eMedicineTopic, MeshName, and MeshNumber. If no InfoBox code exists on the main page, do not add one. 3. Remove the Editor Join template from the coding. 4. Use the SI and SIB templates only if there is no expanded navigation template available. Never include both the SI/SIB template and the expanded navigation template simultaneously. 5. Pay close attention to capitalization. Only capitalize the first letter of page names (e.g., Category:Page name here). Patient Information Page Content: The goal of the page is to provide patient-oriented information that addresses the background, diagnosis, and treatment of the condition. The language should be simple and written at an 8th-grade reading level, avoiding overly technical terminology. Appropriate Content Sections: 1. Overview: Provide a general introduction to the condition. 2. Symptoms: Describe the symptoms associated with the condition. 3. Causes: Explain the underlying causes of the condition. 4. Risk Factors: Identify individuals or groups at the highest risk for developing the condition. 5. Urgent Medical Care: Indicate when patients should seek immediate medical attention. 6. Diagnosis: Outline the diagnostic process for the condition. 7. Treatment Options: Discuss available treatment modalities. 8. Medical Care Locations: Provide information on where patients can find medical care for the condition. 9. Prognosis: Explain what patients can expect in terms of outcomes and recovery. 10. Complications: Highlight potential complications that may arise from the condition. 11. Sources: Include references and sources for the information provided. Additional Instructions: Include a link back to the physician page of WikiDoc at the top of the patient information page. Always place an Editor-In-Chief code at the top of the page. Do not copy content directly from copyrighted sources such as PubMed articles or encyclopedias. Categorization: Assign the page to the Category:Patient information. If the condition pertains to a specific system (e.g., leukemia falls under hematology due to its involvement with the circulatory system), include a category for that system. Once an overview statement is complete, designate the page as Category:Overview complete. Add any additional relevant categories, such as Drug, Disease state, or Surgery, as applicable.
